reader.requirement: At --std 85 the DEPENDING ON operand of a format 2 GO TO must be a numeric elementary data item that is an integer (fixed-point numeric, no digit right of the assumed point; trailing P allowed); a non-integer numeric, alphanumeric, numeric-edited, group, index data item or reference-modified operand is refused, a literal or figurative constant is not an identifier, and at 85 a numeric or integer function-identifier may appear only in an arithmetic expression (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4), so it is refused here too. The witness covers the refusal classes for data items only.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002): below 2002 a numeric or integer function-identifier written as an identifier operand (here identifier-1) is refused COBOL0900; from 2002 it is admitted and classed by its result

reader.edition-search: The data-item path (BindGoTo -> OperandClassScreen.Screen -> ClassesOf/IsIntegerDescription) has no edition input: grepped ControlFlowBinder.cs, OperandClassScreen.cs for Edition|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior; only EditionContext.Error (reporting). The one edition read is on the function-identifier arm, through IntrinsicBinder.IntrinsicOperand.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: a function-identifier identifier-1 (e.g. FUNCTION INTEGER (X)) is refused at 85 (an integer function only in an arithmetic expression, §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4) and admitted from 2002; the data-item screen is the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb212_operand_class_screens covers data-item refusals; not exercised there: the 85 function-identifier refusal, trailing-P integer (PIC 9P) admission, leading-P (PIC P9) refusal, reference-modified operand, and GR3 fall-through at zero/negative/out-of-range values

probes.expected: PIC 9 =2 selects P2; S9(3) COMP =-1, PIC 9 =0 and PIC 9P =20 (integer by description) compile and fall through (GR3); subscripted table element =3 selects Q3

probes.printed: COBOL2324 for WS-D (9V9, not an integer), WS-X (alphanumeric), WS-G (group), WS-ED (numeric-edited), WS-I (index data item), WS-L (PIC P9, not an integer), WS-N (2:1) (reference-modified); plus an unrelated COBOL0900 on VALUE 2 for the numeric-edited item
COBOL5506 unexpected '2' / unexpected 'ZERO' at DEPENDING ON
probes.expected: a literal and a figurative constant are not identifier-1: refused

probes.printed: COBOL0900: a numeric or integer function-identifier where an identifier is written ... requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85) — FUNCTION INTEGER (WS-D)
probes.expected: refused at 85 (integer function only in an arithmetic expression)

probes.printed: COBOL0900 and COBOL2324 for FUNCTION SQRT (WS-D)

OK  §1985:VI.6.15.4 GR3  (6.15.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: The selector is screened by the one operand-class register row GoToDependingSelector over IsIntegerDescription (fixed-point numeric, scale <= 0), so a trailing-P item is admitted and leading-P refused. At 85 a function-identifier never reaches that screen as a legal operand: the 2002 construct row refuses numeric/integer functions outside arithmetic expressions, which matches the 1985 Intrinsic Function amendment.

refuter.evidence: gt_r3.cob (--std 85 --run, exit 0, COMP-P2 / BIG-FALLS / PP-FALLS / P4-QUAL / P5-RENAMES): S9(4) COMP =2 selects P2; PIC 9(18) at its largest value and PIC 9PP =100 (integer by description) compile and fall through (GR3); a qualified WS-Q OF WS-GRP and a 66 RENAMES of one elementary PIC 9 item are admitted and select. gt_r2.cob (--compile-only, exit 65): COBOL2324 for an index-name IX, PIC A, PIC X/X (alphanumeric-edited), 9V99 COMP, an OCCURS group; COBOL2270 for an unsubscripted table element. gt_r4.cob: COBOL2324 for FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:1) (alphanumeric), COBOL0900 for FUNCTION ORD ("A") (integer function outside an arithmetic expression). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.15.3 SR1 'must reference a numeric elementary data item which is an integer'; OK §1985:VI.6.15.4 GR3; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4 'may be used only in an arithmetic expression'. Side observation (not this rule's verdict): the COBOL2324 text for the index-name IX says "'IX' is a numeric function-identifier" (OperandClassScreen.DescribeFunctionResult), a misleading-diagnosis wording; the refusal itself is right.
